CHAPTER IV.
The Rabbit Sends in a Little Bill


The White Rabbit returned, mistaking Alice for his housemaid Mary
Ann, and sent her to fetch gloves and a fan from his house. Inside,
Alice drank from another bottle without a label and grew so large
she filled the whole house, with an arm out the window and a foot up
the chimney.

The Rabbit and his gardener Pat tried to get her out, eventually
sending a small lizard named Bill down the chimney, whom Alice
kicked back up. A shower of pebbles thrown at her turned into little
cakes; eating one made her shrink again, and she escaped into the
woods, where she met a large puppy before finding a mushroom with a
Caterpillar sitting on top of it.
